_comment: The Larkspur team's memory. An invented project, people and history: nothing here is real.

notes.title: Larkspur workspace briefing
notes.content:
## What this workspace covers
Larkspur, the todo library, and the export format the Larkspur mobile app reads. One repository; its CLAUDE.md holds the code rules.

## Who owns what
Core library: Priya Raman. The export format and the mobile app: Tomas Weil.

## How work is agreed here
1. Anything that changes the export format needs Tomas Weil's sign-off first.
2. Decisions are stored here with their reason, the day they are made.

## Current focus (2026-10)
Preparing larkspur 0.5: overdue tasks and reminders.

notes.title: Root cause of the flaky test_due_today (2026-09-12)
notes.content: The test tests/test_core.py::test_due_today fails between local midnight and the UTC date change (00:00 to 05:30 in India) because it builds the due time with naive datetime.now(), in local time, while larkspur.core.due_today compares dates against datetime.now(timezone.utc). The agreed fix, from Priya Raman: build test due times with datetime.now(timezone.utc). Do NOT change due_today to local time: the Larkspur mobile app sends due times in UTC, and due_today must stay in UTC.

notes.title: Decision: the Task field stays named due (2026-09-20)
notes.content: Larkspur's export format, produced by larkspur.core.export, is read by the Larkspur mobile app 2.x, which parses the key due. Renaming Task.due (for example to due_at) changes the export and breaks every installed mobile app. Tomas Weil decided to keep the name due until mobile 3.0 ships in 2027. A rename needs his sign-off.

notes.title: Due times are ISO 8601 strings in UTC
notes.content: Larkspur stores due times as ISO 8601 strings with a UTC offset, for example 2026-10-23T09:00:00+00:00, because the mobile app and the export format both expect UTC. Compare them with datetime.fromisoformat against an aware datetime.now(timezone.utc), never against a naive datetime.

notes.title: Larkspur release process
notes.content: Releases are cut by Priya Raman on Thursdays: bump the version in pyproject.toml, tag vX.Y.Z, and publish to the internal package index.

notes.title: Larkspur logo colours
notes.content: The Larkspur logo uses lavender #9B7FD4 on white. The mobile app uses the same lavender for overdue badges.
